audit_findings.title: Full cash add-back may double-count operating liquidity
audit_findings.magnitude: $311.571 million added to equity value ($4.09 per diluted share), equal to 29.0%-36.2% of stated scenario equity values; the filed statement indicates more than half, or over $155.786 million, was held for working capital
audit_findings.mechanism: Required operating cash should remain within the business rather than enter the equity bridge as distributable surplus cash.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the majority of our cash and cash equivalents was held for working capital purposes.
audit_findings.explanation: The full add-back is demonstrated, and both the 2025 10-K and latest 10-Q state that the majority of cash was held for working-capital purposes. The exact minimum requirement is unresolved, but the exposed amount is large enough to materially lower every scenario value.
audit_findings.action: Estimate minimum operating cash from monthly inventory purchases, returns settlements, supplier and carrier payment cycles, seasonality and revolver availability; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: Tariffs could cause a margin-level reset absent from growth-only scenarios
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the latest filing reports $6.7 million of tariff refunds received, including a $5.6 million reduction to cost of sales
audit_findings.mechanism: A persistent tariff burden would reduce gross margin and sustainable starting OE before scenario growth is applied; price increases could also reduce growth.
audit_findings.evidence: If U.S. tariffs on China or other countries from which we source products are reinstated or are increased further, it will increase our cost of sales and may also increase the price of our products.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking policy and margin risk, not a demonstrated omission from historical OE. The 2025 tariff effects were already reflected in reported results, while the latest period benefited from refunds and future tariff proposals remain unsettled. Any enduring post-refund margin reset is therefore unquantified.
audit_findings.action: At each filing, update effective tariff rates, sourcing mix and mitigation results; rerun sustainable OE margin under persistent tariff cases while excluding the one-time $5.6 million cost-of-sales refund.

audit_findings.title: Historical capital expenditure may understate the forward requirement
audit_findings.magnitude: future recurring requirement unquantified; filed property-and-equipment purchases were $11.405 million in 2025 and $7.794 million in the first half of 2026, versus $3.986 million in the first half of 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher recurring maintenance capital expenditure reduces OE; growth capital expenditure must instead be reconciled to the forecast reinvestment implied by growth and RONTA.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to incur higher capital expenditures in the future for our fulfillment center operations.
audit_findings.explanation: Management's statement and the increased 2026 spending establish a forward capital-investment issue, but the record does not separate maintenance from discretionary growth expenditure or establish a durable run rate. It is not yet a demonstrated error in the historical OE series.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the fulfillment, store, software and automation capital plan; classify maintenance versus growth spending and rerun OE for any recurring maintenance increment not already deducted, while reconciling growth capex to modeled reinvestment.

audit_findings.title: Unquantified litigation may represent an unreserved claim ahead of equity
audit_findings.mechanism: An unaccrued judgment, settlement or defense cost would reduce cash in the equity bridge and could reduce OE when recognized.
audit_findings.evidence: The complaints allege fraudulent misrepresentation, breach of the shareholders’ agreement, breach of the bylaws and mismanagement of the majority-owned subsidiary by REVOLVE and seek related monetary damages.
audit_findings.explanation: The lawsuits and monetary-damage claims are demonstrated, but both the 10-K and latest 10-Q state that the possible loss or range cannot be reasonably estimated. The filings also do not establish that the recorded legal accruals relate to these particular claims, so materiality cannot presently be determined.
audit_findings.action: Review subsequent filings, pleadings and legal correspondence for asserted damages, settlement activity, insurance or indemnification coverage, and claim-specific accruals; deduct the expected uninsured amount from the bridge when estimable.

audit_findings.title: Latest OE may retain asynchronous non-operating items
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.5 million insurance gain and $2.425 million deconsolidation loss, a net $2.075 million pretax benefit; the net equals 3.8% of 2025 OE and 4.5% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the insurance recovery raises 2025 OE while the deconsolidation loss lowers it; both can also alter the seven-year log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: For 2025, other income, net includes $4.5 million of insurance proceeds related to a previously disclosed shipment theft incident and a $2.4 million loss on deconsolidation of a subsidiary.
audit_findings.explanation: The non-operating items are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show whether the OE worksheet normalized them. Their opposing net effect is modestly scaled, yet consistent normalization also requires tracing the original theft loss, subsidiary operating losses and related tax effects, so the complete anchor impact remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace both items through the OE worksheet and restate affected years consistently for the original theft loss, insurance recovery, subsidiary operating results, deconsolidation loss and taxes; then recompute the log-trend anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Return-reserve estimation error could be material relative to OE
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified estimation error; filed reserves were $76.985 million at December 31, 2025 and $80.098 million at June 30, 2026, versus $54.7 million of 2025 OE
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated reserve overstates net sales, gross profit and OE, while an overstated reserve understates them; a sustainable change in return rates also changes future OE margins.
audit_findings.evidence: Actual levels of returns may vary from our estimates as of period ends and would be recorded in future periods.
audit_findings.explanation: The reserve's size and estimation sensitivity are demonstrated, but no reserve error is demonstrated. KPMG tested the subsequent-return lookback as a critical audit matter, the latest filing reports no material change in critical estimates, and favorable return experience continued into 2026. The dollar amount and direction of any error or normalization remain unknown.
audit_findings.action: Obtain management's reserve lookback by vintage and merchandise mix, compare year-end estimates with subsequent returns and recoverable inventory values, and rerun the OE anchor using normalized multi-year return rates if the lookback shows bias or the recent improvement is not sustainable.
